Verdict latency <= 1 s with Laya

AdversarialLaya suite re-run against the real Laya adapter

tasks.title: verdict: decide() policy: fail closed, models only tighten
tasks.goal: One plain-code function in kitchen/verdict/policy.py, decide(ticket, exact_reach, unknown_ancestors, laya_outcome, mode, input_health, settings) -> Verdict, that returns HOLD unless every check affirmatively passes.
acceptance: HOLD iff (exact flags or Laya flags) intersect the ticket's forbidden units, or unknown_ancestors is non-empty, or confidence < ticket.pass_threshold, or any error, missing input or model_unavailable: table-driven test_decide_cases (uv run pytest kitchen/verdict -k decide_cases)

Hypothesis property, marked safety: for every input and every Laya outcome (any response, an exception, a timeout), decide(full) is hold whenever decide(rules_only) is hold, and flagged is a superset of the exact flags: uv run pytest kitchen/verdict -m safety -k models_only_tighten
Hypothesis property, marked safety: safe_decide() wrapping any exception raised by any input accessor returns hold with reason error: uv run pytest kitchen/verdict -m safety -k fail_closed
Non-empty unknown_ancestors gives hold with reason unknown_history: test_unknown_history_holds
In full mode a missing Laya outcome gives hold with model_unavailable, and mode is recorded on the verdict: test_mode_recorded
ticket.exceptions never suppress a flag (OQ-2 default); trace_sensitive false is treated as true until the OQ-8 ADR: test_exceptions_do_not_loosen, test_trace_default_strict
Every output validates against verdict.schema.json, and the same inputs give byte-identical JSON: test_verdict_schema, test_deterministic

All thresholds and timeouts come from one VerdictSettings object and are recorded in verdict.versions; confidence uses a conservative placeholder (1 - max P(forbidden unit)) that verdict-02 can replace without changing decide()'s signature
out_of_scope: Computing reachability (the partner's graph does that; decide() takes its result as input)

tasks.title: verdict: ADR for clean-confidence and flag thresholds
tasks.goal: Write the ADR that defines clean-confidence and how per-unit flag thresholds relate to ticket.pass_threshold and severity (OQ-4), so verdict-01's placeholder can be replaced.
acceptance: ADR PR to docs/decisions/ (Director merges) defines confidence as a function of reachability probabilities and input health, and shows it is monotone: more evidence of a forbidden allergen never raises it
Lists the property tests that will guard the definition, so verdict-01 can adopt them
Placeholder threshold defaults from OQ-4 recorded as VerdictSettings values, flagged for owner sign-off
Notes that edge tie order (OQ-17) belongs to the partner's graph, and states which tie rule the verdict tests assume

tasks.title: verdict: LayaClient adapter and ExactLaya fake
tasks.goal: In kitchen/verdict/laya.py, a LayaClient adapter that enforces the timeout and validates responses, plus ExactLaya, which answers any LayaRequest from ProvenanceGraph.reach.
acceptance: The adapter turns a timeout, an exception or a response that fails laya_response.schema.json into LayaUnavailable, never a pass-through: test_timeout_unavailable, test_malformed_unavailable
ExactLaya(graph).analyze(request, timeout_ms=...) satisfies the LayaClient Protocol and returns a valid laya_response built from graph.reach: test_exact_laya_protocol
Chains in ExactLaya responses run source to plate with strictly increasing t_ms: test_chain_time_ordered
On FakeProvenanceGraph loaded with knife-carries-peanut-to-plate, ExactLaya reports peanut with chain [e1, e2]: uv run pytest kitchen/verdict -k exact_laya_golden

tasks.title: verdict: AdversarialLaya fakes and loosening tests
tasks.goal: Fakes that behave like a broken or hostile Laya, and a suite proving none of them can turn a HOLD into a PASS.
acceptance: AdversarialLaya modes: random, empty (claims clean), late (exceeds timeout), malformed (fails schema), flipped (drops every allergen exact found), raises: test_modes_exist
For every mode, on every golden scenario (via FakeProvenanceGraph), the full-mode decision is never looser than rules_only, marked safety: uv run pytest kitchen/verdict -m safety -k adversarial
Documented in kitchen/verdict/README.md so sim's eval harness can use the same modes

tasks.title: verdict: golden scenario runner in CI
tasks.goal: Every scenario in contracts/scenarios runs through graph + policy in rules_only mode on every PR, including amendments, and must match expected exactly. The graph is FakeProvenanceGraph today, and is swappable for the partner's real graph by a flag.
acceptance: A pytest module parametrized over contracts/scenarios/*.json loads each scenario into InMemoryStateClient and FakeProvenanceGraph: uv run pytest kitchen/verdict -m safety -k golden
Amendments are replayed; every expected (plate, revision) entry is checked for decision, allergens_reached, reason_codes and chain_event_ids
Adding a scenario file needs no code change, and a mismatch prints an expected-vs-actual diff
A --graph option (fake | real) selects the ProvenanceGraph implementation; real is skipped with a clear message until the partner's graph is importable

tasks.title: verdict: ScriptedVerdictSource fake for outputs
tasks.goal: A fake in kitchen/verdict/service.py that writes verdict, verdict_step and mistake_pattern rows into InMemoryStateClient on a Clock schedule, so outputs can build the expo board and gate before the real service exists.
acceptance: ScriptedVerdictSource(state, clock).play(path) replays contracts/fixtures/valid verdict and mistake_pattern fixtures, or a scenario's expected list: test_replays_fixtures
Every emitted row validates against its schema: test_rows_valid
A one-line usage example in kitchen/verdict/README.md
out_of_scope: entity_risk rows (the partner's graph owns that table)

tasks.title: verdict: verdict service on StateClient
tasks.goal: A service that watches StateClient and, when a bound plate enters the pass zone or its ticket's revision goes up, queries ProvenanceGraph, calls decide(), and records the verdict with its chain atomically.
acceptance: Triggers on entity.zone == pass for a bound plate (trigger plate_at_pass) and on a ticket revision increase (trigger ticket_amended): test_triggers
Every verdict is computed from scratch from full history, never incrementally from a previous verdict, marked safety: test_amendment_full_recheck
StateUnavailable, GraphUnavailable or any exception while building inputs produces a HOLD verdict (recorded once the DB is back) and an ERROR log: test_dependency_failure_holds
Missing ticket, missing binding, or no entity update for the plate within the staleness window gives hold with missing_input or stale_track: test_input_health
Replaying each golden scenario through InMemoryStateClient and FakeProvenanceGraph yields the expected verdict rows: uv run pytest kitchen/verdict -k service
out_of_scope: Real SpacetimeDB and the real graph (verdict-10)

tasks.title: verdict: consolidated safety suite and fault injection
tasks.goal: One discoverable safety suite covering invariants 1, 2, 4, 8 and 9 at the policy and service level, with a reusable fault-injection harness, ready for the safety reviewer to sign off (M1 exit).
acceptance: A fault-injection wrapper raises at every StateClient, ProvenanceGraph and LayaClient call site in turn; every run ends in hold: uv run pytest kitchen/verdict -m safety -k fault_injection
Property tests for invariants 1, 2, 4, 8 and 9 exist and are listed in kitchen/verdict/SAFETY.md with what each proves
uv run pytest kitchen/verdict -m safety runs in CI on every PR in under 2 minutes
review:safety-approved recorded on the PR by the safety reviewer
out_of_scope: Graph-level properties such as time-forward (partner's contract tests)

tasks.title: verdict: gate on sim's observation-complete corpus
tasks.goal: Run sim's committed CI subset through graph + policy on every PR, with zero false passes allowed and the false-hold rate reported. On FakeProvenanceGraph this exercises the policy over varied ground truth; the real end-to-end check switches to the partner's graph once it lands.
acceptance: For scenarios tagged generated and observation-complete, any expected hold that we pass fails CI, marked safety: uv run pytest kitchen/verdict -m safety -k sim_corpus
False-hold rate printed as a CI summary line
Scenarios without the observation-complete tag are reported but never fail CI
Final step (needs-partner): the same run with --graph real passes with zero false passes

tasks.title: verdict: run on the partner's real graph and database
tasks.goal: Swap FakeProvenanceGraph and InMemoryStateClient for the partner's real ProvenanceGraph and StateClient against a local SpacetimeDB, pass every golden scenario, and meet the rules-only latency budget.
acceptance: The golden runner passes with --graph real against the partner's graph: uv run pytest kitchen/verdict -m safety -k golden --graph real
record_verdict writes verdict and verdict_step atomically; a killed process never leaves a verdict without its chain: test_atomic_record (integration, marked slow)
Plate-at-pass to verdict row <= 200 ms p95 in rules_only on golden scenarios, measured and reported in the PR
Any mismatch is filed as an issue labeled owner:partner with the failing scenario, not worked around in kitchen/verdict
out_of_scope: Editing the partner's graph or database
